label: Personality
value: The Wizard is resourceful when helping Dorothy and her friends.
unit: The Wizard is a cunning trickster and ventriloquist who relies on deception, theatrical illusions, and clever diplomacy rather than actual magic. Though he is an admitted humbug, he is fundamentally good-natured, compassionate, and anxious to avoid harming anyone. He feels deep remorse for deceiving his subjects, yet he is generous and resourceful when helping Dorothy and her friends. He acts out of self-preservation and fear of being exposed by the wicked witches.

label: Traits
value: Fair-minded

label: History
value: Dorothy lingering in the house to catch Toto resulted in them both being carried away inside the house to the Land of Oz.
unit: Toto lived in Kansas with Dorothy and her family, serving as her constant companion and making her laugh in the gray prairie environment. When a cyclone struck Kansas, Toto hid under the bed, causing Dorothy to linger in the house to catch him, which resulted in them both being carried away inside the house to the Land of Oz. Throughout their journey along the Yellow Brick Road, Toto accompanied Dorothy, making friends with the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Cowardly Lion. He famously tipped over the screen in the Emerald City throne room, revealing that the Wizard was merely an ordinary man from Omaha. After traveling to the South to see Glinda the Good Witch, Toto returned home safely to Kansas with Dorothy when she clicked her Silver Shoes together.

label: Princess Ozma
value: Rival of — Deposed her family's line and gave her as a baby to Mombi to keep his throne

label: Status
value: Deceased or deposed / missing

label: History
value: During the journey, he repeatedly risked his life to save his companions.
unit: The Cowardly Lion first met Dorothy Gale, Toto, the Scarecrow, and the Tin Woodman in a forest along the Yellow Brick Road when he tried to attack Toto, prompting Dorothy to slap his nose. Ashamed of his cowardice, he joined Dorothy's quest to Emerald City in hopes that the Wizard of Oz would grant him courage. During the journey, he repeatedly risked his life to save his companions by leaping across dangerous chasms, carrying them across a river, and holding off wild Kalidahs. Upon reaching the Emerald City, the Wizard promised to grant his request if the party destroyed the Wicked Witch of the West. In the Winkie Country, the Lion was captured and caged by the Witch after refusing to be harnessed like a horse, but Dorothy secretly fed him until the Witch was melted. After returning to the Emerald City, the Wizard gave him a potion from a square green bottle, telling him it was courage, which immediately boosted his confidence. On their subsequent journey to the South, the Lion defeated a monstrous Giant Spider threatening an ancient forest, earning the gratitude of the beasts who declared him their King. Afterwards, he rejoined his friends to visit Glinda and eventually said a tearful goodbye to Dorothy before returning to rule his forest domain.

label: Personality
value: Jinjur lacks bravery when faced with real danger.
unit: Jinjur is ambitious, vain, and fond of luxury, but she lacks true strategic capability or bravery when faced with real danger. She mobilizes the women of Oz through appeals to domestic rebellion and a desire for jewels. Despite her usurping of the throne, she is easily frightened by wild beasts and readily abandons her royal aspirations when forced to return to domestic life.

label: Appearance
value: The Scarecrow is stuffed with straw.
unit: The Scarecrow is a living man made of a suit of blue Munchkin clothes stuffed with straw. His face is painted onto a sack that serves as his head, complete with blue eyes, a nose, and a painted mouth. He wears a pointed blue hat and old boots, and his head is filled with sawdust mixed with pins and needles given to him by Oz to represent brains.

label: History
value: The mouth enabled the Saw-Horse to hold reins.
unit: The Saw-Horse was carved by Tip using a carpenter's bench and brought to life when Tip sprinkled it with the magic Powder of Life to test the spell's effectiveness. After coming to life, the Saw-Horse lacked a mouth until Tip carved one for it, enabling it to talk and hold reins. It served as a fast mount for Tip and Jack Pumpkinhead on their journey to the Emerald City. Along the way, it damaged one of its legs in an accident, which was subsequently repaired by the Tin Woodman using gold plating. The Saw-Horse carried the party through various perils during the revolt against General Jinjur and proved instrumental in helping the travelers escape to Winkie Country and seek aid from Glinda the Good. Ultimately, it assisted in restoring Princess Ozma to the throne of Oz.

label: History
value: With the aid of Glinda the Good Witch, Jinjur was defeated.
unit: Ozma was born as the royal princess of Oz, the daughter of King Pastoria. When the Wizard of Oz took power, he entrusted the infant princess to the old witch Mombi, who transformed her into a boy named Tip to keep her true heritage hidden. Growing up under Mombi's harsh care in the Gillikin Country, Tip had no memory of his former life. Seeking to frighten Mombi, Tip constructed Jack Pumpkinhead and brought him to life using Mombi's Powder of Life. After running away from Mombi, Tip journeyed to the Emerald City, where he helped Jack, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, the Woggle-Bug, and the Gump escape General Jinjur's rebel army. With the aid of Glinda the Good Witch, Jinjur was defeated, and Glinda forced Mombi to confess her secrets. Mombi restored Tip to her original form as Princess Ozma, who then took her rightful throne as the monarch of the Land of Oz.

label: Traits
value: Proud of his high education

label: Personality
value: Uncle Henry is a stern man.
unit: Uncle Henry is a stern, solemn, and quiet man who works tirelessly from morning until night. He takes his duties seriously and rarely shows emotion or laughs. Despite his stern demeanor, he cares deeply for his family and works hard to provide for them.

label: Appearance
value: He aimed to hide his ordinary appearance.
unit: In his true form, he is a little, bald, wrinkled old man who wears ordinary clothes. Before being exposed, he used elaborate illusions to appear as a giant head, a lovely lady, a terrifying beast, or a ball of fire to visitors in his throne room. He maintained an air of grandeur and mystery to hide his ordinary, aging human appearance.

label: Appearance
value: Mombi is depicted as a crooked woman.
unit: Mombi is depicted as an old, wrinkled, and crooked woman with a sharp nose and squinting eyes. She wears plain clothing typical of a Gillikin countrywoman. Her appearance is harsh and unappealing, matching her malicious demeanor.

label: Abilities
value: Immunity to fatigue and pain

value: Ruler of the Land of Oz

label: Personality
value: The Woggle-Bug is extremely proud of his intellectual achievements.
unit: The Woggle-Bug is extremely proud of his education and intellectual achievements, often speaking in an overly polite, pompous, and verbose manner. He delights in using complex vocabulary and making frequent, groaning puns, regardless of whether his companions appreciate them. Despite his vanity and lofty demeanor, he is fundamentally friendly, polite, and loyal to his companions.

label: History
value: Mombi used her newly acquired Powder of Life to bring Jack to life.
unit: Jack Pumpkinhead was carved and built out of branches and a pumpkin by a boy named Tip in the Gillikin Country to frighten the witch Mombi. Instead of being frightened, Mombi used her newly acquired Powder of Life to bring Jack to life as a test. Tip later fled from Mombi's home and brought Jack along, with Jack regarding Tip as his father. Together with the Sawhorse, which was also brought to life by the Powder of Life, they traveled to the Emerald City. Upon arriving, Jack met the Scarecrow, the ruler of Oz, and the two formed a fast friendship due to their shared non-human natures. When General Jinjur's Army of Revolt besieged the Emerald City, Jack accompanied Tip, the Scarecrow, and their companions on a series of escapes and adventures across Oz, culminating in the restoration of Princess Ozma to the throne.

label: Status
value: Alive

label: Personality
value: Glinda is gracious
unit: Glinda is gracious, wise, and profoundly benevolent, dedicated to protecting the people of Oz and administering justice fairly. She remains calm and stately in all situations, using her powerful magic for good rather than personal power. She is generous with her guidance, helping others discover their own strength and capabilities instead of simply solving their problems for them.

label: History
value: Jinjur wears the city's jewels.
unit: General Jinjur raises an Army of Revolt composed entirely of young women armed with knitting needles. Capitalizing on the Scarecrow's absence, she marches on the Emerald City and successfully captures it, forcing the male populace to do housework while the women take control. She crowns herself ruler and spends her days lounging in the palace eating caramels and wearing the city's jewels. When the Scarecrow returns with Tip, Jack Pumpkinhead, and the Sawhorse, Jinjur manages to keep them at bay initially using her army and the help of Mombi. However, when Glinda the Good Arrives with her army and Glinda's allies release fierce animals into the palace, Jinjur and her soldiers panic. After Glinda restores Princess Ozma to the throne, Jinjur abdicates, surrenders her command, and agrees to return home to her household duties.

value: Fear of being separated from Toto

label: History
value: The Tin Woodman was rusted in the forest for a year.
unit: After being rusted in the forest for a year, the Tin Woodman was discovered and oiled by Dorothy Gale and the Scarecrow. He joined Dorothy on her journey along the yellow brick road to the Emerald City, hoping the Wizard of Oz would give him a heart. Along the way, he used his axe to assist the group, chopping down trees and defending them from threats. Upon reaching Oz, the Wizard tasked the companions with defeating the Wicked Witch of the West; during their quest, the Tin Woodman was dropped onto sharp rocks by the Winged Monkeys and battered into tin junk. After Dorothy defeated the Witch, the Winkies repaired the Tin Woodman and invited him to become their ruler, which he accepted after completing his quest. Returning to the Emerald City, he received a velvet-and-sawdust heart from the Wizard. He then helped Dorothy journey to the South to see Glinda. Later, when General Jinjur and her Army of Revolt overthrew the Scarecrow in the Emerald City, the Scarecrow escaped to the West to seek the Tin Woodman's aid. Reunited, they set out to reclaim the throne, eventually forming a party with Tip, Jack Pumpkinhead, the Sawhorse, and the Woggle-Bug, and defeating the rebels with the aid of Glinda.

label: Goals
value: To provide for his wife Aunt Em and his niece Dorothy

label: Appearance
value: Jinjur wears a colorful uniform.
unit: Jinjur is a young Munchkin woman described as being quite pretty. She wears a colorful uniform fashioned to distinguish herself as the leader of her all-female army. She is frequently seen eating knitting needles or snacking on sweetmeats while lounging on the royal throne.

value: Kind-hearted

label: History
value: Tip joins forces with the Woggle-Bug
unit: Tip grows up in the Gillikin Country under the harsh care of the witch Mombi. To frighten Mombi, Tip constructs a man made of pumpkin and wood, naming him Jack Pumpkinhead. Mombi uses the Powder of Life to bring Jack to life, and after Tip learns she intends to turn him into a marble statue, he runs away with Jack. Along their journey, Tip uses the Powder of Life to animate the Sawhorse, which becomes their mount. Arriving at the Emerald City, they find it besieged by General Jinjur and her Army of Revolt. Tip joins forces with the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and later the Woggle-Bug to reclaim the throne. After building the Gump to escape Jinjur's forces, the companions seek the aid of Glinda the Good Sorceress. Glinda discovers that Tip is actually Princess Ozma, the rightful ruler of Oz who was transformed into a boy by Mombi. Glinda forces Mombi to reverse the spell, restoring Tip to her true form as Princess Ozma, who then takes her rightful place on the throne of Oz.

label: Background by volume
value: Settled on the Kansas prairie with his wife, Aunt Em

label: Personality
value: The Tin Woodman worries about causing harm to insects.
unit: Extremely tender-hearted, gentle, and compassionate, the Tin Woodman constantly worries about causing harm to any living creature, even insects. Because he believes he lacks a natural heart, he strives extra hard to be kind and loving. He is deeply loyal to his friends and willing to face danger to protect them. However, he is prone to weeping when moved or saddened, which causes his tin jaws to rust shut if he is not careful.

label: Appearance
value: The Woggle-Bug wears knee breeches.
unit: The Woggle-Bug is a large insect that has been magnified to human size, retaining his insectoid features while standing upright on his hind legs. He wears stylish, tailored human clothing, including a brightly colored coat, knee breeches, striped stockings, and a top hat. His oversized boots and polished cane complete his distinguished, dapper look.

label: History
value: Dorothy lived on a small farm in Kansas
unit: Dorothy lived on a small farm in Kansas with her Aunt Em, Uncle Henry, and her dog Toto until a powerful cyclone swept their farmhouse away into the magical Land of Oz. Upon landing, her house accidentally crushed the Wicked Witch of the East, earning her the gratitude of the Munchkins and the witch's Silver Shoes. Advised by the Good Witch of the North, Dorothy set out along the Yellow Brick Road toward the Emerald City to seek the aid of the Great Wizard of Oz. Along the way, she befriended and recruited the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Cowardly Lion. The Wizard agreed to help her only if she destroyed the Wicked Witch of the West, which Dorothy eventually accomplished by throwing a bucket of water over the witch when she attempted to steal one of Dorothy's Silver Shoes. After discovering the Wizard was a fraud who accidentally departed in a balloon without her, Dorothy journeyed to the South to seek Glinda the Good Witch. Glinda revealed that the magical Silver Shoes had possessed the power to carry her anywhere all along, allowing Dorothy to click her heels three times and safely return home to Kansas.

label: Appearance
value: Toto has soft long hair.
unit: Toto is a small black dog with soft long hair and small black eyes that sparkle merrily. He wears a collar around his neck. His compact size makes him easy to carry, though he is agile and lively.

label: Appearance
value: Dorothy is a little orphan girl.
unit: Dorothy is a little orphan girl with bright eyes and a wholesome, youthful appearance. During her adventures in Oz, she wears a blue-and-white gingham dress given to her by the Munchkins. She notably wore glowing Silver Shoes taken from the Wicked Witch of the East throughout her quest to return home.
